questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country with many opportunities to explore culture and nature and somewhere i hadnt been before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. I received everything by mail

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Usyd gave a list options, which were mostly dorms or shared apartments. Some single rooms and some twin rooms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a big kitechen. No meal plan so you would have too cook yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its very expensiv, but super nice as you get to meet a lot of people including many other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You would have to apply for the university through there system. After that you could apply for a visa and then choose your classes laters.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They sent a mail guiding you through the proccess step by step, except for the visa, which you would have to do by yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont do it last minute, casuse unexpected problems can occur. If there is anything problem reach out to the host universitys coordinator. They were very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The third year bachelor courses are pretty difficult, sop dont take too many of them.
Generally the level is probably pretty similar to KU, but for me the test and exams were a bit different, which i had to get used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Lectures and some practical classes in smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Lagranian and hamiltonian dynamics.
PDE's and waves
Science of australias deadly animals
Introduction to OS and networking

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend "Science of Australias deadly animals" or "learning in outdoor education" if you have electives.
In these course you get to learn about australia while you are there and go on excurision.
They are also not very time consuming, giving you more spare time during your exchange.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The visa and the housing were very expensive.
Public transport is very cheap especially if you get the student concession.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They has a sportscenter, where you could play a lot of different sports. They also had a swimming pool and a gym.

They had a lot of social clubs (more than 100) for people with different interests.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Surfing. You can take classes or just rent a board at the beaches.
I would also highly recommend to go on the surf camp.

The bushwalking club is vcery nice if you like hiking. You get to see much of the nature in and around Sydney.

And lastly i would recommend to go on trips.-

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on trips. There are so many options for both vlong weekend and holiday trips

Cairns and the great barrier reef
Whitsundays
Melbourne
Byron Bay
Uluru
Western Australia is very nice, but you need more time and to hire a car.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. They're isnt a lot of big cultural differences i would say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The beach culture in sydney and the many cultures from all around the world that is found in Sydney.

People talk a lot more to each other, than in europe for instance.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to get into a student accomodation. Its great oppotunity to meet more people.
Dont take too many hard courses. You want to have more spare time to explore Sydney, go out, go to beach and go on trips.
Apply for grants and have savings, cause its expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for student housing immideately when the application window opens. The best places get full within hours.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting many new friends from all around the world and going on trips around Australia with these people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Even though i experienced a lot more than i would in Denmark i still got fomo from some of the things happening at home and missed a lot of people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
